summary: Fix Rust Luby current-round priority filtering and make its GPU hash wrapping arithmetic explicit.
regressions: Both new regressions were first executed against the unmodified Rust CPU oracle and failed with noalias disabled
A four-node conflict clique checks all 24 invocation orders, two priority/tie profiles and both fresh/previously colored states (96 schedules)
129 hash inputs run the actual reset entry point and compare against independent u64 modulo arithmetic
The same regression source is included by the Rust shader test module and the pinned CPU oracle; debug and release tests pass after the fix
differences: Reference bug fix: neighbors colored in the current round remain in the priority comparison; only earlier colors are excluded. This prevents adjacent nodes taking the same current color when one invocation observes another winner.
Reference bug fix: wrapping_mul expresses the existing intended modulo-2^32 GPU hash and prevents checked CPU overflow panics; GPU arithmetic is unchanged.
No floating-point arithmetic or tolerance changes. The TileLang coloring implementation will be added in a subsequent classified record and compared to this corrected reference.
New live Rust coloring fixtures prepare independent reset, flag, step and conflict-pruning phase inputs for that port.
